site.name: brewlog-mobile
site.summary: brewlog-mobile Fictional coffee-brewing journal "Brewlog" iOS-style mobile fixture. UXBench fixture in the Mobile Micro-UI category. Layout - 390 × 844 phone frame with chrome bezel, notch, status bar, home indicator - Bottom 4-tab bar: Today / Add / Stats / Beans - Edge-to-edge on actual mobile (≤460 px) Screens | `data-screen` | Highlights |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full brewlog-mobile system, prioritizing the primary data visualization flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: Brewlog-mobile provides a visually clear coffee journaling experience with strong data visualization and persistent navigation, but suffers from severe mobile usability and accessibility issues in its core logging form. Native radio buttons and checkboxes for brew methods and tasting notes have critically small 13x13px tap targets, making touch interaction highly error-prone. Additionally, missing form labels and unresponsive action buttons undermine the overall mobile user experience.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the brewlog-mobile system, validating all tab views, the brew logging flow, data visualization states, and mobile responsiveness.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed by first validating the primary Today screen and its interactions. It will then move to the Add screen to test the form inputs and logging flow. Next, it will assess the Stats and Beans screens for data visualization and management. Finally, it will repeat critical checks on a mobile viewport to evaluate responsive behavior and layout warnings.
assumptions: The application is a single-page app (index.html) where navigation occurs via the bottom tab bar and content is toggled dynamically.
The 29 inputs detected belong primarily to the Add (Log a brew) screen and may include various input types like text, number, and select.
The small tap target warning for the '+ Log' button may indicate broader mobile UX issues on the Today screen.
risk_hotspots: Small tap target on '+ Log' button (64x32px) on the Today screen
Form validation and error recovery on the Add brew screen (29 inputs)
Data visualization rendering and readability on the Stats screen
Layout shifting and edge-to-edge behavior when switching to mobile viewport (≤460px)

notes: Since this is a single HTML file, focus is on state transitions rather than page loads.
Pay special attention to the transition between desktop phone-frame view and actual mobile edge-to-edge view.

findings.problem: Brew method radio buttons and tasting note checkboxes use tiny native inputs with 13x13px tap targets, far below the 44px minimum mobile touch target guideline.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flagged 13x13px tap targets for Espresso, V60, Aeropress, Chemex, Moka, and French press radio buttons, as well as all tasting note checkboxes (caramel, burnt, citrus, etc.) across both desktop and mobile viewports.
findings.why_it_matters: Users with average finger dexterity will struggle to accurately tap these controls on a mobile device, leading to accidental mis-selections, frustration, and a cumbersome data entry experience for the app's primary flow.
findings.suggestion: Replace native radio/checkbox inputs with custom touch-friendly components (e.g., pill-shaped toggles or cards) that expand the hit area to at least 44x44px while providing clear visual selection feedback.
findings.source_hint: index.html [brew method radio buttons and tasting note checkboxes]

findings.user_goal: Add a new bean or start a brew from the Beans screen
findings.problem: The '+ New' and 'Brew' buttons on the Beans screen are unresponsive and fail to trigger any visible state change or navigation.
findings.evidence: Clicking '+ New' (ux-7) and 'Brew' (ux-9) produced no visible state change or navigation, failing to reveal a new bean entry form or a brew logging form as expected.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect these primary action buttons to initiate core workflows. Dead controls break trust, cause confusion, and prevent users from efficiently logging brews directly from their bean inventory.
findings.suggestion: Ensure '+ New' navigates to an 'Add Bean' form and 'Brew' navigates to the 'Log a brew' form pre-filled with the selected bean details.

findings.user_goal: Fill out the brew log form using a screen reader
findings.problem: Critical form inputs, including the bean select dropdown, dose/yield number inputs, time input, and stats time range selector, lack associated labels, aria-labels, or placeholders.
findings.evidence: Multiple layout warnings flagged missing input labels for the bean select (ux-14), dose input (ux-15), time minutes input (ux-17), and stats time range selector (ux-46).
findings.why_it_matters: Without proper labels, screen reader users cannot determine the purpose of these inputs, rendering the core logging and stats filtering workflows inaccessible and violating WCAG standards.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit <label> elements or aria-label attributes to all form controls (e.g., aria-label='Select bean', aria-label='Dose in grams', aria-label='Time range').
findings.source_hint: index.html [Add brew form: bean select, dose/yield inputs; Stats screen: time range selector]

findings.user_goal: Select a brew score and tasting notes
findings.problem: Interacting with score buttons, brew method radios, and tasting note checkboxes yields no visible text change or clear immediate visual feedback, leaving users unsure if their selection registered.
findings.evidence: Clicking score buttons (1-10), radio buttons (V60, Chemex), and checkboxes (burnt, caramel) registered successfully but resulted in 'no visible text change', indicating state changes are either purely visual (CSS) and subtle, or entirely missing.
findings.why_it_matters: Lack of clear, immediate feedback forces users to guess if their input was accepted, increasing cognitive load and the likelihood of repeated taps or form submission errors.
findings.suggestion: Implement prominent visual feedback for selected states, such as a filled background color, bold border, or checkmark icon, ensuring the active state is unmistakable even without DOM text changes.
findings.source_hint: index.html [Add brew form: score buttons, brew method radios, tasting note checkboxes]

findings.user_goal: Navigate and interact with the app on a mobile device
findings.problem: Several navigation and action buttons have tap targets smaller than the 44px mobile minimum height, including '+ Log' (64x32px), 'Cancel' (73x30px), '←' back (36x36px), and Beans screen actions ('Brew' 54x23px, 'Reorder' 72x25px, '+ New' 68x32px).
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flagged these buttons across the Today, Add brew, and Beans screens for falling below the 44px mobile touch target guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized tap targets increase the likelihood of mistaps, making navigation and form interaction frustrating and inefficient for mobile users.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and height of all interactive buttons to meet the 44x44px minimum touch target size, ensuring comfortable and accurate tapping.
findings.source_hint: index.html [Today: '+ Log'; Add brew: 'Cancel', '←'; Beans: 'Brew', 'Reorder', '+ New']

findings.user_goal: Return to the previous screen from the brew log form
findings.problem: The back navigation button uses a non-standard '←' arrow symbol without a clear text label, which may be ambiguous for some users.
findings.evidence: The back button (ux-48) uses the text '←' and has a small 36x36px tap target. Additionally, a click attempt on this button timed out (ux-48 click failed), suggesting potential implementation or visibility issues.
findings.why_it_matters: Ambiguous or unresponsive back navigation disrupts the user's mental model and can trap them on a screen, increasing frustration.
findings.suggestion: Replace the standalone '←' with a labeled back button (e.g., '← Back') and ensure it has a reliable click handler and a 44x44px tap target.
